newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds pulled down by U.S., losses small.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds pulled down by U.S., losses small.

text.p: Argentine bonds were pulled lower Thursday by sharp declines in U.S. Treasuries but leading issues finished flat or at the most slightly lower.
"The market is going through a small correction but it is nothing serious," said Agustin Etchebarne, chief economist at the C&E consultancy.
Traders said activity was once again fairly slim with few new players emerging in the market.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was down flat at 90-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.05 to 126.30.

Traders said the market was still nervous about the possibility of a negative impact from a court ruling in Brazil Wednesday granting 11 civil servants wage rises of 28.9 percent. The worry is that other public employees will use the ruling as a precedent, something which could lead to a huge bill for the government.
"In spite of that we are positive for the market in the medium-term," said Lourenco.
In the money markets, call money rates were stable at 6.48 percent.
